ing: or salt beef, soaked and rinsed
st: Soak the salted pork in cold water for 1 hour, then drain and cut into chunks. Boil it in fresh water for 15 minutes and drain to remove extra salt.
Peel the breadfruit, remove the core, and cut it into 2-inch chunks.
Mix [[1 cup]] flour with [[0.25 tsp]] salt and about 3 tablespoons water to make a stiff dough. Roll into small finger-shaped dumplings.
In a large heavy pot, layer the pork, chicken, onion, garlic, celery, thyme, and breadfruit.
Pour [[3 cups]] coconut milk and [[2 cups]] water over the top. Add [[1 tsp]] turmeric, the remaining [[0.75 tsp]] salt, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on medium-low for 40 minutes.
Add the dumplings and callaloo on top. Cover and cook for 20 minutes more until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Continue to cook uncovered for 15 minutes until the liquid cooks off and the stew is oily and golden. Stir gently once.
Taste for salt and serve hot.

ing: or spinach with a few collard leaves, chopped
st: Wash the callaloo well and chop the leaves and tender stems. Slice the okra into rounds.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the callaloo, okra, thyme, and [[4 cups]] broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the okra and greens are very soft.
Remove the thyme stems. Blend the soup with an immersion blender until fairly smooth.
Stir in [[1.5 cups]] coconut milk, [[1 tsp]] salt, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat gently for 5 minutes without a hard boil. Taste and serve hot.
Rinse the conch and pound it with a mallet to tenderize. Cut into 1-inch pieces.
Rub with the lime juice, [[1 tbsp]] curry powder, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the conch and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Add the tomatoes, thyme, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Pour in [[3 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 75 minutes until tender.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes to thicken the sauce. Serve with rice or roti.
Soak the salt cod overnight in cold water, changing it once. Drain, then boil in fresh water for 15 minutes. Flake, discarding bones and skin.
Mix [[2.5 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[0.75 cup]] warm water to make a soft dough.
Knead for 3 minutes, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each to a 0.5-inch disk.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the bakes for 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden. Drain.
In a clean pan, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onion and pepper for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the flaked cod for 3 minutes.
Split the warm bakes and fill with the saltfish.
Rinse the fish with water and the juice of the limes, then pat dry.
Put [[6 cups]] water, the onion, garlic, carrot, thyme, and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix [[1 cup]] flour with [[0.25 tsp]] salt and a few tablespoons of water into a stiff dough. Roll into small dumplings.
Drop the dumplings into the broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Lay in the fish and cook gently for 10 minutes, until it flakes at 145°F (63°C).
Season with [[0.25 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, remove the thyme stems, and serve hot.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking powder, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[1 cup]] warm water and knead 5 minutes. Rest for 30 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot, stir in [[2 tbsp]] curry powder for 1 minute, then add the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the potatoes, chickpeas, and [[1.5 cups]] water. Simmer, covered, for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the potatoes are soft.
Mash a few potatoes to thicken, season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and keep warm.
Divide the dough into 4 balls. Roll each into a thin 10-inch round and brush with oil and a sprinkle of [[1 tbsp]] curry powder.
Cook each round in a hot dry skillet for 2 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until blistered. Wrap in a towel.
Spoon filling on each roti, fold the sides in like a burrito, and serve.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] milk, [[1 cup]] cream, and half the sugar in a saucepan until steaming, not boiling. Stir in the nutmeg.
Whisk the yolks with the remaining sugar and the salt until pale.
Slowly pour the hot milk into the yolks while whisking.
Return to the pan and cook over low heat, stirring, for 6 minutes until it coats a spoon and reaches 170°F (77°C). Do not boil.
Strain into a bowl and stir in the remaining [[0.5 cup]] cream and the vanilla.
Chill the custard in the fridge for 4 hours or overnight.
Churn in an ice cream maker for 25 minutes until thick.
Freeze in a covered container for 2 hours until firm. Scoop and serve.
